name: Simon Schreibt
about: Game artist and VFX artist behind the Game Art Tricks blog, which breaks down how classic and modern games achieve their visual effects, with Houdini and Unreal tutorials. In the industry since 2006 and a full-time VFX artist since 2015.

name: Makin' Stuff Look Good
about: Indie game developer formerly known as Makin' Stuff Look Good, teaching Unity visuals, shaders and game programming through YouTube videos.

name: Catlike Coding
about: Jasper Flick's long-running written Unity tutorial series covering rendering, custom SRPs, procedural meshes and gameplay systems, plus Godot tutorials. He is an independent developer in Amsterdam and has written tutorials since 2011.

name: Mix and Jam
about: Game developer and designer behind Mix and Jam, a YouTube channel recreating game mechanics and effects in Unity with downloadable projects.

name: MinionsArt
about: Artist, shader programmer and indie developer who writes approachable Unity shader and VFX tutorials, and is making the cat adventure game Astro Kat.

name: Cyan
about: Hobbyist game developer who writes in-depth Unity shader, Shader Graph and URP tutorials and shares shader experiments.

name: Alan Zucconi
about: Goldsmiths senior lecturer and science communicator known for Unity shader tutorials, machine learning and game development articles. Author of the Unity 5.x Shaders and Effects Cookbook and co-author of the 2018 edition.

name: Harry Alisavakis
about: Technical artist known for approachable shader and VFX tutorials on his blog and the Technically Art newsletter, focused on making games look good with code. Was a technical artist at Jumpship (Somerville) as of 2022.

name: Ronja
about: Creator of Ronja's Tutorials, an approachable written series on Unity HLSL shaders aimed at making shader programming understandable for everyone. Writes code at Chasing Carrots.

name: Febucci
about: Indie developer and tool maker teaching Unity programming and game feel on a blog, and making assets like Text Animator for Unity.

name: Ned Makes Games
about: Game developer and graphics engineer producing Unity shader tutorials in written (Medium) and video form, especially HLSL and URP.

name: Team Dogpit
about: Small game studio whose graphics programmer Xibanya (Manuela Malasaña) wrote the 'Shaders For People Who Don't Know How To Shader' beginner series for Unity.

name: Daniel Ilett
about: Shader and graphics developer who teaches Unity shaders, post-processing and effects through tutorials and videos. Author of Building Quality Shaders for Unity (Apress, 2022).

name: GameDevGuru
about: Unity performance specialist who helps teams find and fix performance bottlenecks, publishing articles and a newsletter on optimization.

name: Lexdev
about: Author of Lexdev Tutorials, in-depth Unity graphics tutorials on compute shaders, deferred rendering and gameplay data visualization.

name: Ming-Lun Chou
about: Game programmer at Naughty Dog (since 2014; Uncharted 4, Uncharted: The Lost Legacy and The Last of Us Part II) who writes technical blog posts on game physics, math, animation and engine programming with Unity examples.

name: Jettelly
about: Game dev education studio publishing Unity and Godot eBooks, video courses and YouTube tutorials on shaders, VFX and graphics.

name: GameDevBill
about: Programmer with over a decade in games who shares Unity learning notes, including a shader series, on a blog and YouTube channel.

name: Freya Holmér
about: Shader and graphics programmer, creator of Shapes and Shader Forge, known for math-heavy visual YouTube explainers and Unity shader and tooling content. Independent developer and co-founder of Neat Corporation (Budget Cuts).

name: Alex Strook
about: French-Canadian indie developer and tech artist (The Spirit and the Mouse, Squeakross) sharing Unity shader, vertex-colour and stylised rendering tips.

name: Ana Opara
about: Procedural artist and co-founder of Pounce Light, co-creator of Tiny Glade; previously researched procedural generation and texture synthesis at EA SEED and Embark.

name: Ben Cloward
about: Shader creation tutorials for Unity and Unreal, from a long-time game developer who co-created the ShaderFX node-based shader tool and has worked on the Shader Graph team at Unity. His Shader Graph Basics series runs to more than 60 episodes, from your first shader to toon looks and post-processing.

name: rob (bobacupcake)
about: Game developer and technical artist who publishes shader walkthroughs and a shader-basics reference on his site, covering sparkles, translucency and stylised materials.

name: Christina Creates Games
about: Unity UI tutorials and game-building guides on YouTube: layout groups, masks, drag-and-drop lists, card systems, the new Input System, UI shaders and modular level design.

name: Code Monkey
about: Professional indie developer (Endless Loop Studios) teaching Unity and C# through free video tutorials and step-by-step courses.

name: Decompiled Art
about: Technical art tutorials on visual effects and shader tricks, with shader and VFX packages for sale.

name: Gabriel Aguiar Prod.
about: YouTube channel teaching game VFX, with Unity VFX Graph tutorials such as muzzle flash, portal, meteor and waterfall effects, plus some Unreal Niagara.

name: Gal Bartouv
about: Unity developer writing about procedural generation, shaders, UI performance, C# architecture and keeping projects tidy, with deep-dives from shipped mobile games and the Privateer prototype.

name: Game Dev Guide
about: YouTube channel with Unity game development tutorials and guidance for aspiring developers.

name: Game Maker's Toolkit
about: Mark Brown's YouTube channel analysing game design, level design and accessibility; he also runs the GMTK Game Jam and made Mind Over Magnet and Word Play.

name: Game Slave
about: Teaches Unity shaders and VFX with Shader Graph tutorials: interactive water and grass, stencil portals, toon and card effects. Some older videos are in Spanish. Writing The Shader Survival Guide, a shaders and VFX book.

name: Gamedev Engine Room
about: YouTube channel on game development with Unity, with a companion studio publishing on GitHub.

name: gamedev:hq
about: YouTube channel and training site offering Unity game development tutorials and free resources.

name: git-amend
about: Advanced Unity tutorials on core mechanics, programming patterns, architecture and software engineering principles.

name: iHeartGameDev
about: Unity programming tutorials: state machines, the Observer and Command patterns, third-person movement, Cinemachine and a free procedural animation course. Last upload was in late 2024, but the tutorials are evergreen.

name: Kristin Lague
about: YouTube creator making Unity game development tutorials and devlogs.

name: LlamAcademy
about: Beginner-friendly and in-depth Unity tutorials covering a wide range of topics, from UI Toolkit to AI and content loading.

name: Matt MirrorFish
about: YouTube creator producing Unity game development tutorials and guides.

name: Oskar Stålberg
about: Swedish indie developer behind Bad North and Townscaper, known for talks on Wave Function Collapse, irregular grids and tile-based procedural generation.

name: Sebastian Lague
about: Game developer behind the Coding Adventure series: long-form videos on simulation, ray tracing, procedural generation and algorithms, with the Unity projects open-sourced on GitHub.

name: Sykoo
about: YouTube creator making Unity game development tutorials and showcases.

name: Tarodev
about: Unity developer who publishes tips on game architecture, C# and project structure, with free project code and a community Discord.

name: Turbo Makes Games
about: Content about building games with data-oriented design: Unity DOTS and ECS, including "The Hot Path" show.

name: Unity
about: Official technical blog posts and free Unity 6 e-books from Unity: rendering, URP/HDRP, VFX Graph, profiling and optimization, UI Toolkit, DOTS and workflows.

name: Keijiro Takahashi
about: Unity technical artist and prolific open-source author: VFX Graph and Shader Graph samples, post effects (Kino), GPU simulations, audio and video I/O plugins, and many small experiments. Based in Tokyo and long associated with Unity Japan.

name: Red Blob Games
about: Amit Patel’s site of interactive tutorials on hex grids, A* pathfinding and procedural map generation. Engine-agnostic and widely used as the reference by game developers, with code samples in several languages including C#.

name: Sakura Rabbit
about: VFX artist and developer known for real-time Unity shader showcases: rain, snow coverage, water and character effects, several built for URP on mobile. Some projects are downloadable. Covered by 80 Level.

name: Nitzan Wilnai
about: Game developer and author of High Performance Unity Game Development (Manning), a book on building games with data-oriented design. His GitHub hosts live DOD benchmarks and Unity examples.

name: Ben Golus
about: Shader and graphics programmer who writes long, careful articles on shader technique: anti-aliased alpha test, triplanar normal mapping, mipmapping, outlines, grids and normal maps. Mostly Unity, and useful well beyond it.

name: Alexander Ameye
about: Writes a personal blog about Unity, shaders, graphics engineering, rendering, technical art and programming, including stylized water and real-time caustics write-ups.

name: Joyrok
about: Writes technical 2D UI experiments and write-ups, including a series on signed distance fields (SDFs) for UI.

name: Boris the Brave
about: Writes about procedural generation, with widely read explanations of Wave Function Collapse and model synthesis.

name: Sawce Games
about: Indie game development group from Brazil that publishes shader studies, such as a Skillshot Arrow shader and a Nier Automata shader study.

name: Habrador (Erik Nordeus)
about: Erik Nordeus writes Unity tutorials, including boat physics and parallax-mapping shaders, and publishes open-source C# projects such as computational geometry, programming patterns and a self-driving vehicle.

name: Torch in Sky
about: Writes Unity stylized VFX and shader-animation tutorials, such as a series on step, smoothstep and dissolve effects.

name: Sebastian Schöner
about: Writes a technical blog on Unity internals, including improving Unity's Mono code generation, managed jobs and profiling.

name: Staggart Creations
about: Unity developer who publishes open-source rendering and editor utilities on GitHub, including a GPU raycaster, a MeshLOD-to-FBX exporter and a terrain layer sampler.

name: Roger Boesch
about: Software architect and engineer in Zürich with 30+ years in mobile and XR, including Magic Leap. Builds retro-console games and tools, and created the Game Mechanics Compendium of 269 game mechanics.

name: Moonjump
about: Independent game studio in Canberra, Australia. Publishes the Mechanics Library: long-form, interactive tutorials on how game systems work, from pathfinding and procedural generation to rendering and physics.

name: Bronson Zgeb
about: Game developer, previously at Unity, KO_OP and Square Enix Montréal. Writes Unity tutorials on ScriptableObject design patterns, custom lighting in Shader Graph, SDFs and procedural generation. His blog has been quiet since 2023, but the articles hold up.

name: Alexandre Mutel (xoofx)
about: Author of the Burst compiler and long-time C#/.NET open-source developer. His blog has deep dives on how Burst works and on running Unity on CoreCLR. His blog is quiet since 2024; most of his current work is general .NET, not Unity.

name: Linden Reid
about: Blog of Unity shader and procedural geometry tutorials, written in ShaderLab/CG for the built-in pipeline between 2017 and 2019: toon shading, dissolves, rim light, waving grass, and an intro series on procedural meshes. The ideas carry over to URP and Shader Graph; the code does not paste in directly.

name: Daniil Spivak
about: 3D technical artist with 10+ years in games, with credits on AAA titles for studios such as id Software, 343 Industries, Ubisoft, Gearbox and BioWare. Write-ups of Unreal Engine materials and shaders (toon, snow, ice, glitter, translucency, post-process outlines) whose techniques carry over to Shader Graph. Also learning Unity.
